name: Arlington Memorial Bridge
note: Roadway is bike-legal end to end and one authority throughout; the midpoint heuristic must not split it.

name: Key Bridge
note: The roadway is a legal, ordinary climb, not barred - riders use it every day. sidepath_only marks it anyway: it is a narrow bridge with no shoulder and no way off mid-span, so a mass ride still has to be kept to the sidewalk provision rather than the traffic lane. Do not read sidepath_only as a legality claim; roadway_bicycle_legal is the legality claim. The DC-Virginia boundary on the Potomac is the 1791 Virginia shoreline, not the channel, so this span lies within the District along essentially its whole length and MPD's jurisdiction runs end to end - the same shape as the Arlington Memorial Bridge row, which is the right shape for every Potomac span. The earlier split down the middle was the midpoint heuristic written into the data. Boundary is a matter of record; the policing that follows from it is community working knowledge, not a legal statement. The Virginia approach ramps beyond the abutment are VDOT's and Arlington County's; the structure is not.

name: Chain Bridge
note: A standard, bike-legal climb out of Georgetown - not barred. Five-foot sidewalk with no way off mid-span is why sidepath_only is still set: a mass ride cannot use the roadway safely even though an individual rider legally can. The DC-Virginia boundary on the Potomac is the 1791 Virginia shoreline, not the channel, so this span lies within the District along essentially its whole length and MPD's jurisdiction runs end to end - the same shape as the Arlington Memorial Bridge row, which is the right shape for every Potomac span. The earlier split down the middle was the midpoint heuristic written into the data. Boundary is a matter of record; the policing that follows from it is community working knowledge, not a legal statement. The row previously named Fairfax County Police for the Virginia end, which was wrong twice over: the Virginia abutment is in Arlington County, not Fairfax, and on the boundary above it is not a Virginia authority's to police at all.

name: George Mason Memorial Bridge
note: One of the five parallel structures at the 14th Street crossing, which this file used to record as three. The five are three highway spans - Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial (1950), George Mason Memorial (1962), Rochambeau (1972) - plus the Long Bridge carrying freight and commuter rail and the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge carrying Metro's Yellow Line. Not one bridge and not one answer, which is why they are separate rows. This one carries I-395's southbound lanes out of the District, and it is where the shared-use path is: the Mount Vernon Trail connection that ramps to Columbia Island on the Virginia side and Ohio Drive SW on the District side is a sidewalk on this highway span, not a structure of its own and not on the Metro bridge. The roadway carries bicycle=no, so roadway_bicycle_legal is false; the path is the only and the intended crossing, so sidepath_only is true. Two claims here are community knowledge rather than record and they are not held at the same confidence. That this span is the one carrying the path is medium-high, from the reviewer who rides it, and it is the one claim a survey could move. The direction is medium-high too and was recorded backwards until round 5: the 1950 Williams span carries the northbound lanes into the District - it is the span Air Florida flight 90 struck - so this 1962 span carries the southbound lanes out of it. Unverified against a real extract.

name: Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial Bridge
osm_names: Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial Bridge
note: One of the five parallel structures at the 14th Street crossing, which this file used to record as three. The five are three highway spans - Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial (1950), George Mason Memorial (1962), Rochambeau (1972) - plus the Long Bridge carrying freight and commuter rail and the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge carrying Metro's Yellow Line. Not one bridge and not one answer, which is why they are separate rows. This row said this was the Metrorail bridge and that it carried the Mount Vernon Trail connection. It is neither. It is the 1950 highway span carrying I-395's northbound lanes into the District - the one Air Florida flight 90 struck in January 1982, renamed in 1985 for the passenger who passed the rescue line to others and drowned. That it is the 1950 span and that it is the span flight 90 struck are matters of record, not OSM questions; which direction it carries is community knowledge at medium-high confidence and was recorded backwards until round 5, as southbound. The Metro crossing is the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge, a separate structure with its own row, and the shared-use path is on the George Mason Memorial Bridge. So this span is bicycle=no on the roadway with no sidepath on it: barred outright, not sidepath-only. Community working knowledge for the OSM spelling, unverified against a real extract.

name: Charles R. Fenwick Bridge
note: One of the five parallel structures at the 14th Street crossing, which this file used to record as three. The five are three highway spans - Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial (1950), George Mason Memorial (1962), Rochambeau (1972) - plus the Long Bridge carrying freight and commuter rail and the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge carrying Metro's Yellow Line. Not one bridge and not one answer, which is why they are separate rows. This is the Metro crossing - the Yellow Line between Pentagon and L'Enfant Plaza - and it was missing from this file entirely while its name sat on the Williams row's note. A Metro bridge carries no roadway and no path: there is no bicycle access of any kind, which is why roadway_bicycle_legal is false and sidepath_only is false together. It is recorded so the structure has a row of its own rather than being rediscovered as somebody else's identity. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: Long Bridge
note: The sixth structure at the 14th Street crossing and the rail one: freight, and the commuter and intercity trains that share it. No roadway and no path. It has a row for exactly the reason the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge has one, and until round 5 it did not - this file stated a rule, "no row for anything rail-only", and then broke it for Fenwick one paragraph later. One rule for both: a structure at a crossing this deployment has an opinion about gets a row, whatever it carries, so that its identity is recorded here rather than rediscovered on somebody else's row. roadway_bicycle_legal and sidepath_only are false together, which is what "no bicycle access of any kind" looks like in these two columns. The name is the most collidable in this file - Arlington has a Long Bridge Park and a Long Bridge Drive - but the match is exact and restricted to bridge-tagged, non-trail-class ways, so a park path or a street named after the bridge is not reachable by it. Ownership is CSX's and row_owner_verified is false: the structure is CSX's, the trains on it are not all CSX's, and this file has not checked which entity holds the right-of-way at either abutment. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: Woodrow Wilson Bridge path
police: Alexandria PD / Prince George's County Police / MPD
note: The roadway carries I-95/I-495 and bicycle=no in OSM; the shared-use path is a separate structure and the only crossing. Three authorities, not two: the Maryland end is in Prince George's County, and the span clips the District itself - the Wilson Bridge is the one Potomac crossing that touches all three - so MPD belongs here alongside Alexandria and Prince George's. row_owner was MDTA and is now MDOT SHA: MDTA is Maryland's toll authority and this bridge is toll-free, which is the tell; MDOT SHA operates it. Medium confidence, and row_owner_verified stays false - ownership of the connecting right-of-way on the Virginia side (the Jones Point sliver, the short-crossing case) may sit with VDOT again.

name: Sousa Bridge (Pennsylvania Avenue SE)
note: Pennsylvania Avenue SE's Anacostia crossing, and one a mass ride can use: a bike-legal roadway, neither barred nor sidepath-only. The row's `name` is this file's own label, written to say which street the bridge carries; OSM's name is the full "John Philip Sousa Bridge", which is what `osm_names` now claims. Until round 5 the row carried no `osm_names` at all, so the label was what the resolver matched on - a string with a parenthesis in it that no OSM way carries, which could only ever miss, and a miss here is silent except in the unmatched log. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

It is also the span most likely to carry the plain name "11th Street Bridge" in OSM, which is what `osm_names` claims. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: Theodore Roosevelt Bridge
note: Carries I-66 across the Potomac; bicycle=no in OSM and no sidepath on the structure, so this is barred outright rather than sidepath-only. Tagged highway=trunk, which MOTOR_ONLY does not catch, so the no-trail variant depends entirely on the rm:bridge_bicycle mechanism (resolve_bridge_bicycle_legality) to keep a mass ride off it - there is no highway-class fallback here. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: American Legion Bridge
police: Montgomery County Police / Maryland State Police
note: Carries the Capital Beltway (I-495) across the Potomac near Cabin John. No bicycle or pedestrian provision of any kind - not sidepath-only, no access. The police column was a split down the middle, Montgomery County and Fairfax County, which is the midpoint heuristic this file exists to override, written into the data. The shoreline reasoning that puts every District span under one authority applies here with the line in a different place: above Washington the Potomac is Maryland's to the Virginia bank, which Virginia v. Maryland (2003) left undisturbed as to the boundary itself while deciding what Virginia may do from its own shore, so this span lies essentially in Maryland along its whole length. Montgomery County Police and the Maryland State Police, then, with Fairfax County reached only at the Virginia approach beyond the abutment - the same shape the Key Bridge row gives VDOT and Arlington County. Boundary is a matter of record; the policing that follows from it is community working knowledge at medium confidence, not a legal statement. row_owner reads MDOT SHA rather than "Maryland SHA", which is the same agency under a spelling this file no longer uses. The alias "George Kennan Memorial Bridge" has been removed: nothing places that name on this structure or on any other crossing in the coverage area, and an unplaceable alias in this file is a name that can only ever match the wrong way. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.
